Margaret Smith Court. An Australian tennis legend who holds the record for most Grand Slam singles titles with twenty-four, surpassing all competitors until Rafael Nadal. Her extraordinary dominance across three decades and her sixty-four Grand Slam titles across all categories make her one of the sport's greatest and most underrated figures. She won eleven Australian Opens, five French Opens, three Wimbledons, and five US Opens for a total of twenty-four Grand Slam singles titles. She won sixty-four Grand Slam titles across singles, doubles, and mixed doubles, the highest total in tennis history. She dominated the 1960s and early 1970s, and her peak years saw her win multiple majors in a single calendar year, nearly achieving a Calendar Slam. Known for her powerful serve and baseline game, her athleticism and competitive intensity were exceptional for her era. She reached world number one in 1963 and held it for 220 weeks, and her consistency across surfaces was remarkable. She won the Australian Open a record eleven times, establishing it as her signature tournament, though her record has been approached by later champions. Her legacy as a dominant force across the entire tennis landscape is unmatched among female players of her generation.
